The statement’s tone is modestly positive on growth and employment but tempered by persistent below‑target inflation and weak business investment/exports. In line with New Keynesian/Taylor‑rule insights (e.g., Clarida, Galí, and Gertler), inflation running below 2% with low market‑based compensation and stable expectations justifies a continued accommodative stance. The FOMC’s decision to hold the funds rate at 1.50–1.75% and set interest on reserves at 1.60%, while continuing Treasury bill purchases and repo operations via the New York Fed, is consistent with the ample‑reserves operating framework discussed in the implementation literature (e.g., Goodfriend) and supports smooth policy transmission rather than signaling tightening. Given solid job gains (Okun‑type linkage to real activity) but soft capex/exports (IS‑side weakness), the overall sentiment is slightly positive with a dovish tilt.
